why_angle: The guides shoppers see list only each tripod's height with the center column raised, or advise checking the column-down height without giving a figure for any model. This page gives the column-down heights of the Ulanzi Zero Y (132.7 cm), Peak Design (130.2 cm) and Manfrotto Befree Advanced (128 cm), from maker and reviewer spec sheets. It also shows that the Sirui Traveler 5C, even at full stretch with its column up, stands only 5.3 cm taller than the Zero Y does with its column down.
must: the best pick is the Ulanzi Zero Y

page.title: Travel Tripod for Camera: Height With the Column Down, Compared
page.h1: Best travel tripod for a camera: how tall each one stands with the center column down
page.desc: Ulanzi Zero Y, Peak Design and Sirui travel tripods compared on the height that stays steady: center column down. Weights, folded lengths, head loads and today's prices.
page.answer: Short answer. For a lightweight travel tripod for a mirrorless camera, the best pick is the Ulanzi Zero Y: with the center column down it still stands 132.7 cm, taller than the Peak Design (130.2 cm), at 1.1 kg. The Sirui Traveler 5C is the budget pick but reaches 138 cm only column up.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Raising the column adds 22 to 24 cm. Zero Y: 156.7 − 132.7 = 24.0 cm. Peak Design: 152.4 − 130.2 = 22.2 cm. Manfrotto Befree Advanced: 151 − 128 = 23 cm.
  • With the column down, the three are within 4.7 cm of each other. 132.7 − 128 = 4.7 cm, so column-down height alone barely separates them.
  • None reaches standing eye level with the column down. Laurence Norah (Finding the Universe) puts eye level at about 60 in (152.4 cm). Even the tallest falls 152.4 − 132.7 = 19.7 cm short.
  • The Sirui Traveler 5C at full height is close to the others with their columns down. 138 − 132.7 = 5.3 cm, and the 5C needs its column raised to get there.
  • Weight. Shutter Muse weighed the Peak Design aluminum at 1,613 g and the Ulanzi F38, which shares the Zero Y's legs, at 1,127 g. 1,613 − 1,127 = 486 g less to carry.
  • Price. $399.95 − $279.95 = $120 less for the Zero Y.
  • Head load. Norah's rule is a rating of at least twice the weight of your camera plus your heaviest lens. Zero Y: 3 kg ÷ 2 = 1.5 kg (5 kg ÷ 2 = 2.5 kg using Ulanzi's overview figure). Peak Design: 9.1 ÷ 2 = 4.55 kg. Sirui 5C: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 kg.

Why the column-down height is the one to compare

A raised center column holds the camera on one thin tube above the legs, which is where a travel tripod flexes. Dan Carr (Shutter Muse) keeps the Peak Design's column collapsed in anything but the calmest wind. Zach Lovell (TechGearLab) found the Sirui 5C's center column wobbly when fully extended. TechGearLab scored the 5C's stability 5.0/10, the Peak Design 7.0 and the Manfrotto Befree Advanced 7.4.

Stiffness. Carr found the Ulanzi tripod "noticeably more stable than the Peak Design tripod at all heights". He also says the F38 and Zero Y share the same legs, weight and height. Ralph Mayhew pressed down on the top of a fully extended Zero Y and a Peak Design carbon, and the Peak Design's legs bent "significantly more". Shutter Muse found no measurable stability difference between the Peak Design's carbon and aluminum versions, so the carbon one only saves weight (1,307 g against 1,613 g).

Where the Zero Y gives ground: the head. Ulanzi's own page lists the ball head at 3 kg in the spec list and 5 kg in the overview. David Lowe (Ridgeline Images) found that the compact ball head tends to slip under heavy loads. The head isn't detachable: to use another head, Ulanzi recommends its separate F38 1/4 center column. Peak Design sells a $29.95 Universal Head Adapter that lets the Travel Tripod take any standard third-party head.

The Manfrotto Befree Advanced (lever kit with the 494 ball head) stands 128 cm with the column down and 151 cm with it up. It weighs 1.59 kg and closes to 40 cm. Its 9 kg safety payload is the only rating here tested to a named standard (UNI/PdR 105:2021). Its 200PL-PRO plate fits both Manfrotto RC2 and Arca-style clamps. Manfrotto's US page lists no price, so compare retailers.

For the smallest pack and the lowest price, the {buy:sirui-traveler-5c-carbon-travel-tripod} folds to 33 cm, and TechGearLab weighed it at 1.9 lb. Keep its column low in wind.

Not recommended

Ulanzi Zero F38, if you use Arca-type plates or L-brackets. It costs $279.95 − $248.75 = $31.20 less than the Zero Y on the same legs. But Shutter Muse lists its quick-release as not Arca-Swiss compatible and its head as rated for 3 kg, so the Zero Y is worth the difference.
